paper_id: Shi et al. - 2009 - Popularity adaptive search in hybrid P2P systems
title: Popularity adaptive search in hybrid P2P systems
motivation: P2P peers frequently join/leave, causing stale popularity statistics that lead to wrong flooding/DHT decisions
problem_framing: How to correctly estimate item popularity in dynamic P2P where replicas constantly change due to peer churn
key_insight: Designate smart nodes to sense network dynamics and tune gossip-obtained popularity values using dynamic rate β
method_signature: Smart nodes monitor peer changes, compute βg, adjust popularity by γ = 1 + βg(Δt - Δt0)
evaluation_criteria: Estimation error, traffic overhead per link, response time
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: PASH suffers from cheating if ratio of malicious nodes exceeds 10%, needs trust management
evidence_for_taste: statistics of replicas will remain unchanged or increase
flooding threshold is set at Tf
thinking_moves: Identify monotonicity bug in prior gossip design (always increases never decreases)
Formalize dynamic rate β as derivative of replica count
Separate concerns: smart nodes for sensing vs. all nodes for gossip
Derive utility decline formulas to prove problem severity
Adaptive sensing period inversely proportional to deviation δβ
extraction_notes: Published by Elsevier in 2008 (available online). Specific journal name not visible in provided text. Yunhao Liu is co-author (b affiliation - HKUST).
